NFL record * Seasons with 20+ sacks: 2 * Most tackles for loss in a season: 39 | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 586 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] | statvalue2 = 114.5 | statlabel3 = [[Pass deflections]] | statvalue3 = 70 | statlabel4 = [[Fumble|Forced fumbles]] | statvalue4 = 27 | statlabel5 = [[Fumble|Fumble recoveries]] | statvalue5 = 17 | pfr = WattJ.00 }} '''Justin James Watt''' (born March 22, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 12 seasons, primarily with the [[Houston Texans]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Central Michigan Chippewas football|Central Michigan Chippewas]] and [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]] and was selected by the Texans in the first round of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. Watt received the [[AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award]] three times in his first five seasons.{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=January 31, 2015 |title=J.J. Watt wins Defensive Player of the Year award |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/j-j-watt-wins-defensive-player-of-the-year-award-0ap3000000466459 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220109081754/https://www.nfl.com/news/j-j-watt-wins-defensive-player-of-the-year-award-0ap3000000466459 |archive-date=January 9, 2022 |access-date=February 19, 2015 |website=NFL.com}} Watt's position was primarily [[defensive end]]. He also took snaps on offense, catching three touchdown passes in 2014. Watt holds the Texans franchise records for sacks and forced fumbles. In 2017, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' named him its [[Sports Illustrated Sportsperson of the Year|Sportsman of the Year]]. Watt is regarded as one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history.{{cite web |last=Posnanski |first=Joe |date=May 11, 2022 |title=Pro Football 101: J.J. Watt]]. ==Early life== Watt was born in [[Pewaukee, Wisconsin]], to parents Connie, a building operations vice president, and John, a firefighter.{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2017 |title=Watt: 'My mom is literally superwoman' |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/watt-my-mom-is-literally-superwoman-19688906 |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=Steelers.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=August 10, 2016 |title=Watt trains as a firefighter with his dad |url=https://www.khou.com/article/sports/nfl/texans/jj-watt/watt-trains-as-a-firefighter-with-his-dad/285-293345627 |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=KHOU.com |language=en-US}} Both of his younger brothers also went on to play in the NFL.{{Cite web |last=Heyen |first=Billy |date=November 26, 2020 |title=Meet J.J. J. Watt]] plays [[outside linebacker]] for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. Watt played [[ice hockey]] from age four to 13{{Cite web |last=Schumacher |first=Ashley |date=August 24, 2014 |title=My Three Sons: Badger Mom Proud of Watt Brothers On, Off Field |url=https://www.uwalumni.com/news/badger-mom-connie-watt/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106152127/https://www.uwalumni.com/news/badger-mom-connie-watt/ |archive-date=November 6, 2019 |access-date=December 11, 2019 |website=UW Alumni}} and played for travel or competitive teams that traveled to [[Canada]] and [[Germany]]. He gave up hockey when weekly games started to conflict with his schedule and for financial reasons.{{Cite web |last=Pinchevsky |first=Tal |date=September 5, 2013 |title=NFL star J.J. Watt maintains love for hockey |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=681464 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130907020041/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=681464 |archive-date=September 7, 2013 |access-date=November 29, 2014 |website=NHL.com}} Watt also played football throughout his childhood and became passionate about the sport while he was in the fifth grade. Watt attended [[Pewaukee High School]], where he was a four-year letter-winner in [[high school football|football]] and also lettered in basketball, baseball, and track and field.{{Cite web |date=October 25, 2013 |title=Texans' J.J. Watt has high school jersey retired at Pewaukee (Photos) |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/H1uWT5iNy0yfYNw5DN425A/texans-jj-watt-has-high-school-jersey-retired-at-pewaukee-(photos).htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106152119/https://www.maxpreps.com/news/H1uWT5iNy0yfYNw5DN425A/texans-jj-watt-has-high-school-jersey-retired-at-pewaukee-(photos).htm |archive-date=November 6, 2019 |access-date=December 11, 2019 |website=MaxPreps.com}} Watt earned the Woodland Conference Player of the Year Award as a senior, and first-team All-State, All-County, All-Area, and All-Conference selections as [[tight end]] and defensive end. He was also named the team's MVP.{{Cite web |title=J.J. Watt on the sidelines.jpg|thumb|Watt on the sidelines at [[Camp Randall Stadium]] in 2010]] ===Central Michigan=== Watt received a scholarship offer from [[Central Michigan University]]. He has stated that he was led to believe by [[Butch Jones]] that, as a [[tight end]], he would have the opportunity to score touchdowns. He played 14 games with the [[Central Michigan Chippewas football|Chippewas]], compiling 77 receiving yards and 8 receptions.{{Cite web |title=J.J. Watt College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204195236/http://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1.html |archive-date=December 4, 2014 |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=J.J. Watt 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1/gamelog/2007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180219090325/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1/gamelog/2007/ |archive-date=February 19, 2018 |access-date=February 18, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} Watt's coaches, led by Jones, suggested that he move to [[offensive tackle]], but Watt decided to forgo his starting spot and scholarship to [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] the University of Wisconsin–Madison, where he played as a defensive end.{{Cite web |last=Warber |first=Kyle |date=March 24, 2010 |title=Fire Up Chips Exclusive: JJ Watt sets the record straight |url=http://blog.mlive.com/fireupchips/2010/03/jj_watt_sets_the_record_straig.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205010547/http://blog.mlive.com/fireupchips/2010/03/jj_watt_sets_the_record_straig.html |archive-date=December 5, 2014 |access-date=November 29, 2014 |website=MLive |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]]}} ===Wisconsin=== At the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], Watt [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the 2008 season and was named Wisconsin's Scout Team Player of the Year.{{Cite web |last=Rittenberg |first=Adam |author-link=Adam Rittenberg |date=December 30, 2010 |title=Badgers' Watt driven by dreams, hard work |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/bigten/post/_/id/21586/badgers-watt-driven-by-dreams-hard-work |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} In 2009, he played in 13 games as a defensive end for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Badgers]]. In a game against the [[2009 Hawaii Warriors football team|Hawaii Warriors]] on December 5, Watt had a career-high of two sacks, three tackles for loss, six tackles, and one quarterback hurry.{{Cite web |title=Wisconsin at Hawaii Box Score, December 5, 2009 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2009-12-05-hawaii.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008221915/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2009-12-05-hawaii.html |archive-date=October 8, 2022 |access-date=October 8, 2022 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}} Watt finished the season with 32 solo tackles, 12 assisted tackles, four and a half sacks, 15.5 tackles for loss, and five passes defended.{{Cite web |title=J.J. Watt 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1/gamelog/2009/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180219090330/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1/gamelog/2009/ |archive-date=February 19, 2018 |access-date=February 18, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} He also earned his first [[Varsity letter|letter]]. On November 20, 2010, against the [[2010 Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], he recorded his first collegiate interception.{{Cite web |title=Wisconsin at Michigan Box Score, November 20, 2010 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-11-20-michigan.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180219090320/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-11-20-michigan.html |archive-date=February 19, 2018 |access-date=February 18, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} Overall, in the 2010 season, Watt played in 13 games and led the team in tackles for loss, quarterback hurries, blocked kicks, and forced fumbles. He finished the season with 42 solo tackles, 20 assisted tackles, 21 tackles for loss, seven sacks, one interception for 15 yards, nine passes defended, and three fumbles forced.{{Cite web |title=J.J. Watt 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1/gamelog/2010/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180219031326/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/jj-watt-1/gamelog/2010/ |archive-date=February 19, 2018 |access-date=February 18, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} He earned the [[Lott Trophy]] in 2010, voted AP and ''Sports Illustrated'' [[2010 College Football All-America Team|second-team All-American]], All-Big Ten first-team, academic All-Big Ten, and was voted the team's MVP.{{Cite web |title=Ronnie Lott Trophy Winners |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/awards/lott.html |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Pre-draft=== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 5 3/8 | weight = 290 | dash = 4.84 | ten split = 1.71 | twenty split = 2.85 | shuttle = 4.21 | cone drill = 6.88 | vertical = 37 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 0 | bench = 34 | wonderlic = 31{{Cite web |last=McGinn |first=Bob |date=April 16, 2011 |title=State NFL draft prospects |url=http://archive.jsonline.com/sports/packers/119987524.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420232949/http://archive.jsonline.com/sports/packers/119987524.html |archive-date=April 20, 2018 |access-date=April 20, 2018 |website=JSOnline.com}} | arm span = 34 | hand span = 11 1/8 | wingspan ft = 6 | wingspan in = 10 1/2 | note = All values are from [[NFL Scouting Combine]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/j-j-watt/32005741-5457-9210-c7bb-fd19d17d4962 |title=J.J. Justin James  Watt (born March 22, 1989) is an American former professional football player who was a defensive end in the National Football League (NFL) for 12 seasons, primarily with the Houston Texans. He played college football for the Central Michigan Chippewas and Wisconsin Badgers and was selected by the Texans in the first round of the 2011 NFL draft.
Watt received the AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award three times in his first five seasons. Watt's position was primarily defensive end. He also took snaps on offense, catching three touchdown passes in 2014. Watt holds the Texans franchise records for sacks and forced fumbles. In 2017, Sports Illustrated named him its Sportsman of the Year. Watt is regarded as one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history.
After retiring in 2022, Watt joined CBS Sports, working initially as a studio analyst on The NFL Today and then joining Ian Eagle on the network's #2 game announcing team in 2025. Watt is the older brother of Derek Watt and T. J. Watt.
